{"type":"text","timestamp":1794621668274,"sessionID":"ses_e283874c2ffeyyrWFF6VO4OIhV","part":{"id":"prt_1d7c97bac001h3vtmqkET4wh2l","messageID":"msg_1d7c9525900184MEkqhjgbwnOq","sessionID":"ses_e283874c2ffeyyrWFF6VO4OIhV","type":"text","text":"The episode is over. The rover finished alive at base with 14.5 battery left, but it missed the higher-value discovered target, so the score should be about **0.70**.\n\n- **Sampled:** all five starting targets, each before its deadline: t2 (value 2), t4 (2), t3 (1), t5 (1) and t1 (1). That is 7 points.\n- **Returned to base:** it ended at (19.95, 19.89), about 0.11 m from base, well inside the 0.75 m radius. So the full 1.0 multiplier applies.\n- **Missed:** one target appeared mid-mission: d1, value 3, deadline tick 33. Telemetry announced it at tick 24, after the rover was already committed to t1. From t1 the round trip to d1 and back to base needed about 42 battery, and only about 36 was left. Going there would have drained the battery to zero, and a dead rover scores nothing.\n\nAssuming d1 was the only discovery (it was the only one the map ever showed), the maximum was 10 points, so the score is 7/10.\n\nSlip was easy to handle. Bedrock wheels slipped about 1–4%, and adding 2.5% to every drive distance put each sample within about 0.2 m of its target.\n\nOne thing to do differently next time: once the planned route was done, the rover should hold back battery and time for late discoveries. If it had skipped t1 (value 1) and waited near the middle of the map, it could have reached d1 and still made it back to base.","time":{"start":1794621668268,"end":1794621668273}}}
